To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
pulsatile pulmonary arterial flow alters the distribution of pulmonary blood flow in a frequency dependent manner.
the transmission of pulsatile flow through the blood vessels of an isolated lung is frequency dependent, and that this affects the distribution of blood in the lung.
the pattern of flow in the lung is altered when the lung is perfused with blood under pulsatile conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of pulsatile pulmonary arterial pressure on the distribution of pulmonary blood flow.
the effects of pulsatile flow on the distribution of blood to the lung and its effect on gas exchange.
the effects of the frequency of the pulsatile flow in the pulmonary circulation on the distribution of blood in the lung.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the pulmonary circulation is a low-pass filter and the lung is a high-pass filter.
the pulmonary arterial pressure pulsation has a significant effect upon the distribution of blood in the lung, and that this effect is dependent on the frequency of the pulse.
the distribution of blood through the lung is altered by the pulsation of the pulmonary arterial blood pressure and that the degree of alteration is related to the frequency of the pressure pulse.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the distribution of pulmonary blood flow in the isolated lung is altered by the transmission of the pressure wave through the blood vessels.
the distribution of blood to the upper zones of a dog's lung is increased by increasing the pulsation frequency in the pulmonary artery.
the pulmonary artery pressure wave is not only transmitted to the lung but also affects the distribution of blood in the pulmonary vascular bed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pulsatile flow is important for the distribution of blood in the lung, and it is not a passive process.
the lung is not simply a passive recipient of blood flow, but rather a highly active organ that can influence the distribution of blood within itself.
the distribution of blood in the lung is not static, and that it changes with the frequency of the pressure pulse.
